findings.text: GOVERNANCE JUDGMENT (the approved-seed question, step 5). The seed .warp/architecture.yaml is authored status: approved with approved_by: dmitry / approved_at: 2026-07-22. My judgment: this is a DEFENSIBLE-BUT-GENEROUS reading that leans toward over-attestation, and is NOT materially wrong, so it is notes-level, not blocking. It leans over-attestation because the founder approved PLAN-0011 (the intent to build a contract, whose O1 outcome is 'this repository carries its own approved contract as the first instance') but did NOT explicitly review the specific architectural CONTENT the machine authored in this same commit: the 8-area decomposition (contracts/enforcement/loop/fleet/metrics/tracker/distribution/runners), the specific dependency allow-list edges (e.g. fleet->loop, tracker->metrics), and the budget thresholds (1000 file lines, 120 function lines, 8 duplication, 20 complexity). Recording approved_by: dmitry against machine-authored content he did not specifically review is the kind of self-approval-by-proxy NG2 cautions against. It is NOT blocking because: (1) O1's measure explicitly calls for an approved first-instance contract and the founder approved the plan including O1; (2) the builder transparently FLAGGED this exact concern in the manifest assumptions and offered the draft alternative (the opposite of a hidden over-claim); (3) I confirmed status: draft with no approver validates clean (validate_contract rc 0) and the full gate still passes, so a more honest default is one line away; (4) nothing consumes the contract for enforcement yet (first consumers are WARP-1102/W2 and WARP-1103/W3) and the shipped-flip remains a human/orchestrator decision. RECOMMENDATION: dmitry should either explicitly confirm approval of the seed's specific shape (the 8 areas + the dependency graph + the budget numbers) or let the seed enter as status: draft pending that explicit act; draft would be the more defensible default and merely defers O1's approved-first-instance measure.

HONESTY / mechanizable-label nuance (non-blocking). The manifest assumption states 'no rule is marked mechanizable that nothing can yet refuse', but the module_lines budget (kind file_lines, max 1000) is marked mechanizable while NO gate check enforces it against the source today - I confirmed the only consumers of file_lines/module_lines are arch.py's BUDGET_KINDS vocabulary and the selftest, and arch.py's docstring explicitly states it 'does not yet check the source against the contract (that gate enforcement is WARP-1102, W2)'. So the manifest's blanket justification sentence overstates for file_lines. This does NOT violate NG5 and is not blocking: 'mechanizable' is a correct classification of the rule's NATURE (a machine can count file lines with pure stdlib, unlike the AST-dependent function_lines/duplication/complexity which are honestly 'review' until the D6 analyzers ship in W2), the contract's own header is transparent that enforcement of the mechanizable rules against source lands in W2, and W1 carries NO source-shape gate check at all so nothing vacuous is run. The two mechanizable rules the manifest claims are 'already enforced today' check out: engine_byte_identical is enforced by check_pack_drift.py + check_template_sync.sh, and derived_never_authoritative by check_generated.sh (both independent of the contract). Note the contract mixes two flavors of 'mechanizable' (already-enforced-elsewhere vs enforceable-in-W2); the artifact is honest, only the manifest's summarizing sentence is imprecise.

Environmental parity (non-blocking, general to WARP commits). The 'generated' gate check is green today because specs/index.md was regenerated at this commit ('Generated 2026-07-22'); a rerun on a later day would flip it RED until the index is restamped, the same date-stamp behavior recorded in prior WARP-100x reviews.
